rules:
Work only inside this workspace.
The file named in the task is your answer. Edit it in place.
You may write and run your own tests with Icarus Verilog.
Do not use the network or web search.
Do not look for tests, reference solutions or grading files. None are provided.
instructions:
## Knowledge base

A knowledge base built from earlier debugging tasks is available at `/kb`. An agent like you wrote it. After each of those tasks it was shown how its answer had been graded and what the correct fix was, and it wrote with that in front of it. Those were different designs with different bugs, so judge for yourself what carries over to this one. It may be empty.

Look at it before you start work on the task, using the conventions below.

**Entries are notes.** A note is a markdown file holding one lesson, in whatever form suits it. Say what you tried that did not work as well as what did, when the note applies, and which task it came from (the module and the kind of bug). Add a note only when a task taught you something worth keeping, and revise an existing note in preference to adding a near-duplicate.

**Entries are separate files** under `/kb/entries`, found by meaning instead of by name. Run `kbsearch query "what you are looking for" /kb/entries` to list the entries closest in meaning, with their paths, and open the ones that look relevant. New and changed files are picked up the next time a query runs, so adding an entry needs nothing more than writing its file.
update_prompt:
The task is finished and your answer has been graded. The result is above.

Now update the knowledge base at `/kb` so that it is more useful for the next task, which will be a different design with a different bug. Record what the result shows, not what you expected. Follow the conventions you were given for what an entry is and how entries are arranged, and keep any index consistent with the entries. If the task taught you nothing worth keeping and the conventions do not require an entry, change nothing.
